items.basis: The proposed mechanism relies on the polymeric scale-inhibitor coating interfering with calcium carbonate nucleation on the wall surface, but the candidate fails to address the issue of biological growth in the recirculated water, which is a significant contributor to nozzle clogging. The candidate's own evidence bundle is empty, but industry knowledge suggests that biological growth is a major problem in cooling-water systems, and the proposed mechanism does not account for this.

The candidate specifies a water residence time of approximately 1-2 ms in each throat, but this is an extremely short time frame for the proposed coating to be effective. The coating is electrostatically applied and has a thickness of 40 microns, which suggests that it would take significantly longer than 1-2 ms to be fully effective. This boundary condition is likely to be violated, rendering the proposed mechanism ineffective.

The candidate claims that the testable prediction is a 90 percent reduction in adherent scale mass after 120 hours, but this is contradicted by the fact that the proposed coating is only 40 microns thick and would likely be worn away by scale fines in a matter of hours, not days. This contradicts the predicted effect and suggests that the proposed mechanism is unlikely to be effective.

The candidate claims that the proposed solution will reduce clogging events per campaign from 4.1 to below 0.6, but this is equivalent to the baseline condition, which is simply doing nothing new. The candidate fails to provide any evidence that the proposed solution will provide any significant improvement over the current system, and the predicted effect is essentially equivalent to the baseline.

The candidate proposes electrostatically applying a 40-micron layer of phosphonate-embedded polymer coating to all 120 nozzle throats at each scheduled cleaning, but this is an extremely difficult and likely impossible task. The nozzle throats are likely to be in hard-to-reach locations, and the coating process would require significant equipment and expertise. The candidate fails to provide any details on how this would be implemented in practice.

The candidate proposes measuring the effect of the proposed solution by comparing the mass of adherent scale on coated versus uncoated coupons after 120 hours, but this measurement is ambiguous. The coupons may not accurately represent the conditions in the nozzle throats, and the measurement may not capture the full range of effects that the proposed solution is intended to address.
